correctness.rationale: A complete elementary factorization of the hard-core partition polynomial yields monotone imaginary-axis phases and exact roots. An explicit strictly positive implicit-derivative expression proves that all simple axis crossings go left-to-right; polynomial root continuity gives the global count. The threshold envelope has a unique minimizing frequency from a scalar monotonic equation; cycle weight moments sum a=n and sum a^2=3n, plus phase lattice spacing, prove the sharp sqrt(3e n) law. Direct finite independent-set enumeration and exact rational Routh checks supply independent computational crosschecks, not infinite proof.

evidence: Brown–Cameron Corollary 2.2 covers existence of RHP roots for large joined cliques, but not exact thresholds or all parameter values.
Jerrum–Patel 2026 prove degree-bounded zero-free regions around the positive real axis rather than an exact global half-plane count for a graph with unbounded-degree clique hubs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader-looking theorem is inapplicable when degree must remain bounded; the strongest applicable existing claim only implies eventual instability, not the precise theorem.

originality.rationale: The closest broad result (Brown–Cameron, Corollary 2.2) gives only eventual nonstability when a sufficiently large clique joins a cycle with independence number at least four; it has no exact finite-clique count or sharp sqrt(n) transition. The close published equal-root pencil (1+z)^k+r z has different spectral factors and cannot supply the cycle-specific phase list or constant sqrt(3e). The examined related constant-shift wheel spectrum I(C_n;z)+t is not a linear clique perturbation. No dominating statement found in the actual literature and publication searches; independent priority check remains open.
residual_risks: The exact cycle threshold may have appeared in older unindexed independence-root or control-theory literature.
The general left-to-right crossing lemma is elementary and might be known under a different algebraic or Hermite–Biehler formulation.
Not independently peer reviewed or audited; the published near-identical equal-root phase diagram makes the method non-novel even though the cycle theorem and constant are not covered.

value.rationale: Determines a natural finite-family hard-core zero-free boundary in full for all cycle lengths and all clique sizes; sharpens an earlier qualitative clique-join result into exact RHP and boundary multiplicity counts, identifies the first unstable cycle length n=8, and proves the nontrivial critical scaling u*=sqrt(3e n)(1+O(1/n)). This is a motivated complex-zero stability question, not an arbitrary coefficient calculation.
